question: My API supports different ways to authenticate. Can users switch between authentication methods while trying out endpoints? Do their credentials stay saved if they navigate to other pages? Most importantly, where is that sensitive data stored?
ground_truth: When your OpenAPI spec defines multiple authentication schemes, the API Explorer automatically displays them in a dropdown menu, allowing users to select and configure their preferred authentication method before sending requests. Users can switch between auth methods at any time during their session. Once a user sets their authentication credentials, they persist throughout the entire exploration session, even if they navigate to different pages within the docs and return to the API Explorer. From a security perspective, authentication credentials are stored exclusively client-side using cookies - no sensitive user information is collected or stored on Fern's servers, addressing your security concerns. The credentials remain in the user's browser and are used only for making API requests directly from their machine to your API endpoints.
